entities.summary: Pearlite is a two-phased, lamellar structure composed of alternating layers of ferrite and cementite that occurs in some steels and cast irons. This description of alternating layers is not strictly correct, each pearlite colony consists of an bicrystal of interpenetrating layers. A good analogy is a cabbage in a bucket of water, where all the leaves (cementite) are connected, but so is the water (ferrite). It is in two-dimensional sections that the appearance is of alternating layers. During slow cooling of an iron-carbon alloy, pearlite forms by a eutectoid reaction as austenite cools below 727 °C (1,341 °F).
